newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Sept inflation seen by most below 5.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Manila Sept inflation seen by most below 5.5 pct.

text.p: The Philippines' year-on-year inflation for the month of September is expected to fall below 5.5 percent, down from 7.9 percent in August, according to a majority of analysts polled by Reuters on Tuesday.
Stock brokerages were among the more optimistic in their forecasts while a mutual fund thought inflation in September would be between 6.4 to 6.5 percent.
Philippine inflation has been on a downtrend since spiking up to above 11 percent in September last year because of a rice shortage. The rate was 8.9 percent in July.
Noel Reyes, research head of brokerage Anscor Hagedorn Securities forecast September inflation in a range of 4.8 to 5.2 percent.
Alvin Ang, economist at brokerage All Asia Capital, said he expected inflation at 5.1 percent while Erwin Tan, research manager at brokers Abacus Securities, predicted a range of 5.0 to 5.5 percent.

Those predicting that inflation would below 5.5 percent cited their reasons as stabilising rice prices coming from the onset of the harvest and also a "base-effect", meaning the prices base had got distorted last year by a series of typhoons and an acute rice shortage.
But Joby de Belen, general manager of Meridian Securities Inc which runs the Philequity Fund, said he expected inflation at 6.4 to 6.5 percent.
"If I see anything lower than six (percent) I'll be happy," de Belen said, adding that his forecast was higher because he thought the recent oil price increases would affect prices.
"Many people think, the price increases in oil have been very minor and six percent (inflation) is a good target but in reality it could be different, 6.4 to 6.5 percent."
On August 8, Philippine Central bank governor Gabriel Singson had said he expected inflation in September to fall below 6.5 percent.
He had issued his inflation forecast for September to allay fears of a possible jump in prices caused by an oil price increase.
The government is scheduled to release inflation figures on Saturday.
